To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the CuTe films were successfully prepared by co-reduction of copper and tellurium ions in ChCl-EG ionic liquid.
the Cu2Te compound was formed on the Pt electrode at −0.5 to −0.6 V, whereas the CuTe compound was formed at −0.8 V.
Cu2Te and Cu0.656–Te0.344 films have been successfully synthesized on Pt electrode by co-reduction of TeO2 and CuCl in ChCl-EG ionic liquid at 60°C.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation of copper telluride films by co-reduction of Te(IV) and Cu(I) ions in choline chloride-ethylene glycol ionic liquid.
the preparation of copper telluride films by co-reduction of dissolved Cu+ and TeO2 ions in ChCl-EG ionic liquid.
the development of a new ionic liquid electrolyte system for the preparation of CuTe films via co-reduction of the corresponding metal ions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the co-reduction of the Cu+ and TeO2 ions in the ChCl-EG ionic liquid can produce Cu2Te and CuTe phases, depending on the applied cathodic potential and CuCl concentration in the ionic liquid.
the ChCl-EG ionic liquid is a suitable electrolyte for the cathodic co-reduction of copper and tellurium ions and the preparation of copper telluride films.
the ChCl-EG ionic liquid can be considered as a promising electrolytic system for the electrodeposition of CuTe films.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ChCl-EG ionic liquid can be successfully used to electrochemically prepare CuTe thin films.
the ChCl-EG ionic liquid is a good solvent for the preparation of CuTe films via electrodeposition of Cu(I) ions and Te(IV).
the co-deposition of copper and tellurium from ChCl-ionic liquid electrolyte is a promising method for preparing CuTe films.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ChCl-EG ionic liquid can be considered as an alternative solvent to conventional organic solvents in the preparation of CuTe films.
it is possible to prepare CuTe films from a Cu(1+) and Te(IV)-containing ionic liquid at 60°C using a simple potentiostatic technique.
ChCl-EG ionic liquid can be used as a background electrolyte to deposit CuTe films by direct co-reduction.
